chiang-mai.overview: Northern Thailand's best walking is in Doi Inthanon National Park, home to Thailand's highest peak. There, the guided Kew Mae Pan nature trail is a short ridge loop near the summit road, with views over the Mae Pan valley, often above a sea of cloud. Doi Suthep, above Chiang Mai, has forest trails past Monthathan Waterfall. The best walking is from November to January, when the air is clear and the Kew Mae Pan trail is open.

months.7: Heavy rains continue to saturate the ground. The Kew Mae Pan trail stays closed, leaving only lower, muddy forest walks.
months.9: The wettest weather persists, keeping the Kew Mae Pan trail closed and making the open jungle routes muddy and humid.

colombian-caribbean.overview: The famous multi-day route is the Ciudad Perdida, a hot, humid jungle trek of four to six days and roughly 30 miles through the Sierra Nevada foothills to ancient ruins, which requires an authorized guide. Day hikers flock to Tayrona National Park, where well-maintained and busy boardwalk trails transport tourists and locals through the coastal jungle to pristine boulder-strewn beaches. The dry months from December to April offer the best trail conditions.

croatia.overview: The Dalmatian Coast landscape is defined by rugged karst mountains rising straight from the Adriatic, with the best walking found in the limestone gorges of Paklenica National Park and the high ridges of Mount Biokovo. Inland, boardwalks weave through the waterfalls of Plitvice Lakes, a busy destination requiring timed tickets in summer. Most routes are day hikes ranging from easy coastal paths to steep, rocky ascents that demand sturdy footwear.

everglades.overview: Walking in Everglades National Park is primarily on standalone paved paths and elevated boardwalks. The Anhinga Trail and the Shark Valley loop lead into the sawgrass marshes and hardwood hammocks to see alligators and wading birds up close. The dry season is the walking season; summer brings intense heat, flooded paths, and severe mosquitoes.
